Ethylene Dibromide EDB; Etileno, dibromuro de. 1,2-Dibromoethane. C2H4Br2 = 187.9. CAS — 106-93-4. Profile Ethylene dibromide is an insecticidal fumigant and a lead scav- enger used in the petroleum industry. Its use has been restricted in certain areas because of carcinogenicity in animals and be- cause of evidence of persistence in fruit and cereals that have un- dergone fumigation. Ethylene dibromide is more toxic than carbon tetrachloride or ethylene dichloride. It is irritant to the eyes, skin, and mucous membranes. Inhalation leads to drowsiness, CNS depression, and possibly pulmonary oedema. Contact with the skin causes blistering and it is readily absorbed. Kidney and liver damage may occur. ◊ Reports of poisoning due to ethylene dibromide. 1. Letz GA, et al. Two fatalities after acute occupational exposure to ethylene dibromide.
